speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We must ensure that there are robust standards for ensuring the well-being of the child.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can Minister share what requirements it will set to ensure that facilities in the authorised area are appropriate for keeping a child?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: By what standards will immigration officers be held to ensure that they handle a child appropriately?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can Minister also share whether there is any limit to how long a child may be kept in the authorised area?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Digitalisation and automation will help fortify our border security even as we speed up and simplify the immigration clearance process.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We can substantially cut processing time, eliminate mistakes, improve the entire experience for passengers and reduce some of the tedious work for our immigration officers by utilising technology.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This move will place us at the forefront of international practices for immigration processes, in addition to strengthening the security of our borders.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On the other hand, with increasing reliance on digitalisation and biometrics, there will be higher risks from system vulnerabilities and failures.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Every day we receive reports about hacking and data breaches, affecting organisations across sectors and at all levels.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Digital connectivity means that now we need to defend our systems from attackers from around the world, not just at our borders.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Physical copies of permits and passes still have their place as they are immune to hacking attacks, power failures and equipment malfunction.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If biometric data breaches occur, personal identities can be stolen and the hackers can gain access to all aspects of the targets’ lives.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Another concern I have is regarding the inability to use biometric data, especially due to ageing.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Singapore is a fast-ageing society, but so are many other countries.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For some seniors, fingerprints can no longer be read well by scanners due to dry and worn-out skin.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Eyes affected by cataracts or post-cataract surgeries may affect the effectiveness of iris scans.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Next, our immigration system has been under a great deal of stress due to the world witnessing unprecedented challenges, such as pandemics.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I support measures to enable ICA to establish processes to control the entry or transit of persons for reasons of public health.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We need to tighten border security measures to keep these unwelcomed persons as far from our border as possible.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Doing so will reduce the time and manpower demands to process and subsequently send away these foreigners.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, due to the high number of passengers travelling between Malaysia and Singapore every day, there is a possibility that persons impersonating others will try to slip through.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will the Ministry share with House the measures to counter these criminals?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With that, I conclude with my support for the Bill.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: I note this Bill introduces new provisions to support the use of new technologies and innovation to tackle an evolving security landscape.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: It takes into account learnings from the recent pandemic, factored use of digital technologies to improve both effectiveness and efficiency of border operations.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore was early in reopening our boarders in 2022.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Given the rebound of travel, it is timely for this Bill to be put before this House.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: These amendments will not only enable ICA to strengthen immigration controls but also help in its delivery of a more seamless checkpoint experience for residents and tourists.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: These steps will also help upkeep Singapore as a globally reputed transport and tourism hub.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: As such, I support this Bill but would like to seek some clarifications.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: With technology being at the core of this new operating model, any disruption to this critical system, will have considerable risk and costs that include security, reputational and financial.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Given the technology risk around resiliency, can the Minister elaborate on the measures and safeguards to ensure service availability and the expected system uptime?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: As system outages can be expected, can Minister also clarify the plans for redundancy and recoverability?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: For example, will sufficient ICA officers and related resources be available on standby to support an activation of manual clearance processes where required and what kind of tolerable service levels is being planned so that travellers can expect that the system should it not be available?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Regarding the access by the airport operator to biometric and flight information, can Minister elaborate on the measures and the safeguards against misuse, unlawful retention and cybersecurity risks?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: What are the level of governance standards around data usage applicable to ensure robust requirements across different organisations like Changi Airport and airline operators who may have differing data infrastructure and, therefore, security policies as well compared to, say, ICA?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: And will there be independent checks or audits by qualified authorities to ensure compliance?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: While I support the expanded collection of these data to strengthen our border controls, I note that there have been operational difficulties in this regard, where a number of airlines have failed to comply with the requirements to submit advance information to ICA since the inception of advance passenger screening in October 2019.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Can Minister clarify if ICA had sought to understand the root cause of these non-compliances and whether there are plans to improve or smoothen this reporting regime, other than by introducing a composition framework?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Also, considering that the bus operator sector is more fragmented than the airline industry, they also have customer management systems that are less sophisticated and there are ground concerns that such operators may face difficulties with compliance.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: With this ground challenge known, how can ICA ensure the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of information submitted as well as compliance with any issued NBD by bus operators?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Are there plans for ICA to create a generic portal to help such operators to comply with the new regulations?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Clause 8 also expands the powers of the Minister to prohibit the entry or transit by foreigners on public security or public health grounds.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: In this regard, especially in considering PRs who are more likely to have families in Singapore, of which some of whom may even be our citizens, can the Minister clarify the factors of assessment before the exercise of such powers and if there is a lead time for notification so that such affected persons and their families can make adequate preparations?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: In recognising the closure of this gap, may I also seek the Minister's clarification on the number of cases and the total amount of repatriation costs unrecovered over the past five years?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, the Bill seeks to streamline processes regarding the loss and renewal of a PR status as well as the imposing and varying of PR conditions.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: I agree with the underlying principle that the right to enter or stay in Singapore must be the prerogative of the Government.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: On this note, will ICA consider publishing high level guidelines on its assessment criteria to provide some clarity and, more importantly, to guide expected behaviour?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: It is paramount that Singapore recognises these challenges, acknowledges the evolution of technology used for such activities and emphasises the urgency of staying ahead of emerging threats.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: As such, we must harness innovation and technology to enhance our immigration and border management systems.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: In a world marked by unprecedented mobility, criminals and those with malicious intent are using technology to exploit gaps in our immigration and customs control systems.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: The ease with which digital documents can be forged and manipulated poses a grave risk to national security.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: We must remain vigilant and proactive in our efforts to combat these threats.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Criminals are increasingly adept at circumventing traditional controls and our response must be swift, sophisticated and technologically advanced.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Over the years, our immigration technology has evolved, adapting to the changing landscape of threats.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Introducing biometric data such as fingerprints and facial recognition has strengthened our ability to verify identities accurately.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: These technologies are robust deterrents against false identities and those attempting to slip through the cracks.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Furthermore, the advent of electronic passports and identity cards embedded with chips has become a standard practice, ensuring the integrity of our identity documents.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: However, as technology continues to advance, so do the methods employed by criminals.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: We have been using technology integration such as Automated Passport Systems, which expedite entry for legitimate travellers while maintaining a high level of security.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Additionally, advanced data analytics has enabled us to detect patterns and anomalies, enabling us to thwart potential threats in realtime.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: INTERPOL's Stolen and Lost Travel Documents (SLTD) database contains information on travel and identity documents that have been reported as stolen, lost, revoked or invalid.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: First, it is fundamental proof that the existing physical travel document is vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: The physical document holds critical information that is too slow to adapt and use new data points for verification and validation.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Second, the sheer existence of 99 million potential travel identity documents that nefarious and dangerous individuals can use.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: We must better safeguard ourselves and our loved ones.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: The pre-journey bulk submission will reduce the risk for all travellers.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: It would have prevented those potentially dangerous from embarking at the start of the journey.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Embracing technology, digitalisation and innovation is our best defense against false and stolen identities.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: By staying at the forefront of technological advancements, we can ensure our immigration and border systems remain robust and capable of detecting these threats faster and more effectively.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: In the UK, more than 20,000 fake documents have been identified over a decade.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: At the same time, it is paramount that we prioritise privacy and personal rights as we employ technology to bolster security.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Robust data protection measures and transparent practices will ensure that our citizens' rights are safeguarded.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Singapore continues to be at the front edge of technology to ensure that the best possible set of technologies is used to digitalise and automate our processes.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: This is an essential part of the system.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Here, I would like to thank our frontline immigration officers who have served us well all year around 24/7 and have kept Singapore safe.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: First, given the increased data collection and usage, what are the cybersecurity measures taken to enhance the integrity and security of the data?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Second, how do we detect system malfunctions where border entry approvals were wrongly granted?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Second Minister for Home Affairs Mrs Josephine Teo.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Please allow me to address their questions in turn.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Where digitalisation and automated immigration clearance is concerned, there are three broad buckets of concerns.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The first has to do with cyber readiness and resilience; the second on data security; and the third, how we deal with impersonations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Derrick Goh, Mr Desmond Choo, Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Mr Gerald Giam, Mr Shawn Huang, Mr Vikram Nair and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked many good questions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Poh Li San knows the issues particularly well, being deeply involved in airport management.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Besides Dubai, which already offers passport-free clearance for certain enrolled travellers, we do not know exactly which other countries have similar plans.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: MHA and ICA will certainly seek to enable more convenient travel for our people but it is likely that physical passports will still be required for many countries outside of Singapore.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Besides levelling up staff capabilities, the key to a successful implementation of the NCC is universal coverage of all travellers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This requires a willingness to phase out traditional methods of identifying and authenticating travellers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The alternative of running two systems in parallel is not only costly but also cumbersome.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To assist seniors who may not be able to provide certain biometrics or who may not be digitally savvy, I assure Mr Gan, Mr Giam and Mr Yip that immigration officers will be on hand to help.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The officers can also conduct manual clearance by exception.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As immigration clearance becomes more digitalised, ICA is fully aware of its responsibility in ensuring the availability and resilience of its systems.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It therefore works closely with the Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX) and GovTech to meet reliability and security requirements in upstream design.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, the next generation Automated Border Clearance System (ABCS) will allow travellers to continue using automated clearance gates if there are any outages.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is possible because they will be equipped with failover capabilities such as UPS or uninterruptible power supply and can still function if the supporting systems such as the online biometrics database is down.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Nonetheless, some of the NCC capabilities are novel and highly customised to Singapore's context.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Despite our best efforts, disruptions may still happen.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our business continuity plans will then be promptly activated through a combination of measures such as recalling off-duty officers and prioritising traveller clearance according to departure times.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is also the careful approach as we undertake the ongoing upgrade of the Multi-Modal Biometrics System (MMBS), which Mr Giam asked about.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In addition, ICA monitors systems performance to ensure benchmarks are met.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With large systems, external vendors may be involved.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To Ms Poh's query, only Singapore-registered companies can undertake IT projects related to ICA.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: All employees of vendors undergo a compulsory security screening exercise and must be cleared before they are allowed to work on the project.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are bound by a non-disclosure agreement and may be held criminally liable for any wrongful or unauthorised communication, possession or use of information under the relevant laws such as the Public Sector (Governance) Act.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To uphold high standards of cybersecurity, HTX also carries out independent Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing exercises prior to commissioning and annually thereafter.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This complements the regular audits by ICA to identify and address vulnerabilities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I hope Mr Vikram Nair will be reassured to know that ICA will also deploy more advanced scanning technologies and sensors to automate security checks for vehicles.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Additionally, AI will also be used to strengthen detection capabilities for cargo.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These assurances are relevant for both cyber and data security.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Minister’s approval is required for access to and disclosure of data, and must satisfy the purposes specified in the Act, such as for the enforcement of criminal law, failing which an offence can be made out.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In addition, the data will be encrypted and go through secured data exchange gateways.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Specific to the biometric-enabled departure journey at Changi Airport that Mr Derrick Goh asked about, the Changi Airport Group (CAG) will be bound by the terms of a data sharing agreement with ICA.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It puts the onus on CAG to take all reasonable measures to ensure the data is protected against unauthorised access, use, disclosure, modification or misuse.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This includes setting up relevant access controls such as Two-Factor Authentication.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: ICA will audit CAG’s compliance and conduct regular checks on CAG’s systems.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members will be reassured to know that ICA itself must also comply with data protection provisions set out in the Public Sector (Governance) Act and the Instruction Manual 8.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It will retain traveller data only for the period necessary for immigration processing, analytics or investigation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Once these tasks are completed and ICA no longer needs the data, they will be de-personalised and properly deleted.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the unlikely event of a data breach, ICA and HTX will immediately conduct investigations to stop the breach, trace the extent of the breach, and prevent further breaches through remediation measures.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On top of that, system vendors are obliged to adhere to data protection, cybersecurity and breach procedures as part of their contractual obligations to ICA, and must extend full cooperation and assistance to ICA at no additional cost.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Whether with analogue or digital systems, a determined criminal may still try to breach immigration controls.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: ICA will deploy monitoring tools to constantly check on its systems.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are equipped with the capability to detect impersonation and forged or tampered passports presented for clearance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh will be glad to know that the more recent use of multi-modal biometric clearance systems has in fact resulted in better detection of individuals seeking to impersonate others.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For manual clearance, immigration officers are trained to conduct facial checks to ensure that the person is the rightful holder of the passport.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For those undeterred and caught, we will deal with them firmly.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The risk of entry approvals being wrongly granted, which Mr Shawn Huang asked about, is no higher with the NCC than with the current system.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Moreover, ICA and HTX will conduct thorough end-to-end testing for any system changes before deployment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Individuals no longer need to visit ICA to collect the physical card, nor run the risk of losing or damaging it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: ICA will not issue new physical cards for Long-Term Pass Holders but previously issued cards will remain valid until they expire or are cancelled.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: ICA will digitalise other pass types in due course.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If an individual does not have a smart electronic device to display his digital permit or pass, he can enlist the help of family members to access the digital documents from ICA’s e-Services and print a copy to be used at our checkpoints.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As such, we do not expect the digitalisation of passes to cause congestion.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Next, I will go on to ICA’s future-proofing initiatives.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked about the root cause of non-compliance by airlines in submitting advance passenger information.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: From ICA’s experience, it usually boils down to tardiness.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Without being able to screen incoming travellers before their arrival, immigration clearance will be slower.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: A composition framework is therefore necessary, and is already practised in established jurisdictions like the US, the UK and New Zealand.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On the provisions for buses to also collect advance passenger information, let me assure Mr Desmond Choo, Mr Derrick Goh, Ms Poh Li San and Mr Yip Hon Weng that no timeline has been fixed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: ICA has been engaging bus operators since July 2022, and will continue to do so before firming up any plans to collect such information.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Similarly for the NBDs, raised by Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Yip Hon Weng, we will continue discussions with the operators to find a practicable way forward before proceeding.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is premature to go into details but in the event of non-compliance, ICA intends to make a holistic assessment of the facts of the case before deciding whether to prosecute.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The offence of failing to comply with NBDs will likely be compoundable; and this can be provided for in subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Murali Pillai and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about public transport operators such as SBS Transit.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is because tickets are not being sold in advance and advance passenger information thus cannot be collected for ICA’s screening.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Desmond Choo also asked for data on undesirable travellers transiting through our checkpoints.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With an NBD regime, we could keep such undesirable travelers from even coming to Singapore, especially those who pose a high security risk.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Transport operators such as the airlines could also save resources from having to repatriate these travellers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As a final point on NBDs, let me assure Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Yip Hon Weng that ICA will provide adequate transition periods for the respective domains and will do so in close consultation with the industry.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, with the airlines, ICA intends to run trials from end-2024.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked how ICA plans to monitor and validate the accuracy of such statements.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: ICA will review the historical records of a person’s self-declarations and conduct further checks when there are inconsistencies across records.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: ICA will also cross-check with other available sources.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For persons who are suspected to have made false statements or provided false information, ICA will commence investigations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the event passengers fail to declare symptoms of a contagious disease, whether deliberately or otherwise, ICA will work with relevant stakeholders to ensure there are other means to identify them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This includes engaging the transport operators’ help to flag them prior to boarding.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: During a pandemic situation, travellers may also be required to conduct pre-arrival health checks or tests.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If, unfortunately, such passengers still manage to arrive at our checkpoints, ICA will work with the Ministry of Health (MOH) to implement necessary measures to identify them promptly, such as through temperature screening or visual checks.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In terms of enforcement measures, ICA will maintain a firm and strict posture.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Travellers deemed to have made false statements will have their entry into Singapore denied.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With the proposed amendment at clause 57, it will be a strict liability offence for anyone who gives false or misleading information, or omits anything so as to mislead.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked for factors of assessment before the exercise of powers to prohibit the entry or transit of foreigners.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As I have mentioned earlier, we will only use such powers when the situation warrants it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The key consideration is whether such a restriction is proportionate to the severity of the situation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have seen how in times of a pandemic, travel restrictions may have to be put in place at very short notice.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I shall move on to the proposals to strengthen our border controls.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked for the number of cases and the costs unrecovered from repatriated persons over the past five years.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Most of the involved offenders genuinely could not pay their way; the rest were able to.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked two questions on the proposed amendments to introduce fines in lieu of caning, for offenders exempted from or found medically unfit for caning.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To clarify, the law today requires offenders convicted of this offence to be caned.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But for offenders who cannot be caned because of their age or sex, the current law also requires the Court to impose fines in lieu of caning.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is under section 57(1B), which we are not changing.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This allows for the deterrent effect of the penalty to still be met without unduly expending our prison resources while the penalty is held in a suspended state.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Such a move also ensures consistent treatment in offences where fines are imposed in lieu of caning.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Nevertheless, we have decided that this should be left to the Court’s discretion, looking at all the factors in each case.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If the Court considers that an in-default imprisonment term is appropriate, it can also calibrate the length of the imprisonment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Section 319 only sets out the upper limit of the imprisonment terms that can be imposed and do not prevent the Court from imposing a shorter term.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Currently, parties who wish to inform ICA of any Restraining Orders or provide their written consent can do so by simply emailing ICA at a stipulated email address.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is the process we have agreed with the Family Justice Courts and it is set out in the Family Justice Practice Directions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will continuously explore new ways to make the process more efficient.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Louis Ng asked if the facilities in ICA’s authorised area are appropriate for keeping a child.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The new section 5AA seeks to give ICA ancillary powers to keep the child temporarily, while preventing the child from being brought out of Singapore by any person without the consent of the parent or guardian.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: While ICA facilities are not specially designed for a child, it will make all reasonable efforts to ensure the child’s safety and well-being.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Whenever possible, immigration officers will ask that the travelling companion stays with the child until the child’s parent or guardian arrives.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If a child is abandoned at the checkpoints, and the parent or guardian is uncontactable, ICA will hand over the child to the Police.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Child Protection Services will also be involved if necessary.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Murali Pillai spoke about the issue of fairness in dealing with foreigners and asked why there is a need to remove statutory appeals.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As is the case in most countries, foreigners do not have the right to enter or remain in Singapore.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That follows then that they should not be entitled to challenge the terms of their entry or stay under the law.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This position is reflected in our legal provisions regarding the issuance and cancellation of long-term passes and application for citizenship.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There has never been a right of statutory appeal for such immigration facilities and this has also not prevented us from according the affected foreigners fair and reasonable treatment and protection from harm under prevailing laws.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The provision of statutory appeals for entry permit holders who are PRs is found in the Immigration Act 1959, an old piece of legislation dating back to the start of self-government.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are now simply updating and rationalising our laws so that the position for entry permit holders who are PRs is aligned with that of applicants for long-term passes and citizenship.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Like him, we are particularly sympathetic to foreigners with close family ties to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Immigration decisions take into consideration a wide range of factors.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In some cases, this includes sensitive intelligence information.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As I mentioned earlier, each decision is also based on a polycentric evaluation of factors relating to our policies and security needs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: While we understand the desire for explicit reasons to be provided, a blanket provision will be too blunt.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Instead, we will continue to allow foreigners affected by an immigration decision to make representations and to provide explanations to the authorities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As Mr Gerald Giam suggested, for certain decisions, ICA does advise affected persons in broad terms why a decision was made, for example, that his PR status was revoked because of his criminal offences.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Foreigners can continue to seek ICA's reconsideration of the matter and ICA will escalate the matter for the Minister's determination if appropriate.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This approach strikes a better balance between the need to safeguard the public interest and our national security on the one hand and fairness to foreigners affected by immigration decisions on the other.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Gerald Giam asked how affected persons can submit appeals.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They can do so via a general feedback form on ICA's website and it will be directed to the relevant immigration officers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In any case, I can assure them that even without a Member of Parliament's representation, these appeals are attended to.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Giam asked about the administration of the Pre-Marriage LTVP Assessment (PMLA).

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is outside the scope of this Bill but we would like to assure the Member that the Registry of Marriages and the Registry of Muslim Marriages do provide to couples in person advice to complete the PMLA before marriage.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Derrick Goh and Mr Gerald Giam asked immigration criteria can be made more transparent, including the assessment criteria for the renewal of the Re-Entry Permit.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Vikram Nair asked if we can give assurance to law-abiding PRs of their stay in Singapore.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As Members know, we do not disclose our detailed immigration criteria.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are also not the focus of today's Bill.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Nonetheless, I should point out that the comparison with COMPASS neglects important differences.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I was the Manpower Minister when COMPASS was conceived.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Its considerations are that employment pass holders mainly impact the workplace and they are also mostly transient.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But for PRs and Singapore Citizens, the applicants must be considered differently because they are not transient and they impact the wider fabric of society.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Therefore, the considerations must be more holistic and sensitive to long-term impact.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We must also recognise the stronger incentives to game the system if the criteria were fully disclosed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Be that as it may, we have shared the broad criteria that ICA considers, such as whether an applicant is gainfully employed, contributing to Singapore or has family roots here.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: PRs who have conducted themselves well and continue to be a resident in Singapore should not have much difficulty with the renewal of their Re-Entry Permit.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I can assure the Members that the vast majority of applications for Re-Entry Permit renewal are approved.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On the powers of the Controller to publish changes to permit and pass conditions on a prescribed website or by Gazette, Mr Louis Ng asked when such situations would arise.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are many instances where ICA may impose conditions on permit and pass holders.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, if an individual committed a minor offence or displayed adverse behaviour, ICA would notify the person individually that it will impose a condition that he shall not engage in such activities further or risk having his permit or pass cancelled.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: However, there may also be situations where ICA is required to impose conditions en masse, for instance, during a pandemic.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Given the large number of PRs and pass holders, it would not be practicable to contact each and every one to notify them individually.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Controller will then publish the changes on a prescribed website or by Gazette.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Louis Ng rightly pointed out that many individuals may not know how to access a prescribed website or the Gazette.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Hence, ICA will explore suitable avenues to reach out to as many affected persons as possible, for example, through media platforms.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is not the focus of the Bill today and I would draw the Member's attention to ICA's various announcements over the past months on its efforts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Nevertheless, I shall share broadly four key initiatives.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: One, since January 2023, ICA has implemented the Automated Clearance Initiative to allow eligible foreign visitors to use the automated lanes for immigration clearance, without prior enrolment of their biometrics.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Two, ICA will progressively implement automated clearance for cars at the two checkpoints in addition to motorcycles, thereby reducing overall time taken to clear immigration.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Once again, I thank Members for their support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: I think I heard the Minister say that for security reasons, the sharing of Singaporean passengers' biometric data with foreign governments is not on the cards yet.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: This suggests that it may be on the cards in future.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Can I ask if the Government will seek Parliament's approval before the sharing of such personal data with foreign governments in the future?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: And secondly, regarding providing the reasons for rejections of immigration passes, can ICA minimally share the broad criteria that is already been shared in Parliament in their standard rejection letters to applicants so that applicants can figure out on their own where they fell short?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is really just too early for us to even contemplate such a step.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To his second question, I am very sympathetic to the situations when the applicants are told that what they would like to see by way of a grant of permanent residency or other passes has not been approved.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In my own experience dealing with these applicants, even when the reasons are articulated to them, whether broadly or with a fair amount of detail, the disappointment does not go away.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I will be quite realistic as to what these steps can achieve.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think it is more important to look at it in broader context.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.10 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.46 pm until 4.10 pm.
